newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Contentious seminar on Indonesian leader cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Contentious seminar on Indonesian leader cancelled.

text.p: The Indonesian government on Monday cancelled its controversial plan to hold a seminar to reassess the role of the country's first president Sukarno in a failed 1965 coup.

"After we listened to various leaders we proposed to the president that we do not need to hold the Nawaksara seminar which would have been held on June 28," Youth and Sports Minister Haryono Isman said after visiting President Suharto.
"It will not happen. It has been cancelled," Isman said without elaborating.
Isman had proposed the seminar, originally to be held in April. The government had decided to delay the seminar until the May general elections were over.

The seminar, approved by Suharto, was to focus on Sukarno's final public speech in 1966, known as Nawaksara, in which Sukarno denied any links to the abortive 1965 coup which was blamed on the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI).

Suharto, one of the few senior generals to survive the coup attempt, took control of the country and subsequently crushed the Communist party. He initially supported the seminar to explain historic events to the nation's youth.
Hundreds of thousands of communists were killed in military-sponsored programmes in the wake of the coup.
